claims.text: The rider ended the booking at 11:21:10, and the trip record's dropoff_amended_at is 11:21:10 to the second: the dropoff point was amended at the very moment she got out, which the driver himself concedes in his statement ('The booking endpoint was changed at that point, but the app continued recording my car'). The chat shows why — the driver's MSG-00714-001 at 11:20:10 reads 'Add fifteen for the second person or get down', and her MSG-00714-002 at 11:21:10 reads 'We are getting out here. End our booking at this stop', read by the driver at 11:21:35. The journey the platform priced is therefore not the journey booked, and POL-RD-05 requires the optimal route to be re-applied against the amended endpoints.

The SGD 16.80 billed is a fare for a drive the rider was not on. The driver's track runs 121 fixes over 10.8 km from 11:18:40 to 11:38:40, while the rider's own track reports 106 fixes at 0.0 kph from 11:21:10 to 11:38:40 — stationary for the last 17.5 minutes of the 20-minute trip — and the fare charges for exactly 10.8 km and 20.0 minutes. POL-RD-11 confines what may be collected from a rider on an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip to the amount properly chargeable to her; a fare computed over an empty car for the stretch after she ended the booking is not shown anywhere on this record to be chargeable to her.

The record cannot re-price this trip, and the policy says so in terms: trip_record.dropoff_amended_at is non-null while trip_record.amended_optimal_distance_km is null (and amended_optimal_duration_min is null). POL-RD-05 provides that where an amendment timestamp is present but the amended optimal is null, the re-quote is missing from the record, the clause cannot be run, POL-RD-10(5) applies, and the Judge must not derive a substitute figure. With the baseline for the journey actually driven absent, the contested SGD 16.80 cannot be validated either way, and POL-RD-10(5) makes escalation mandatory and terminal: the disputed amount is held rather than collected. That is the outcome the rider asks for.

The driver's endpoint explanation is an uncited assertion and cannot fill that gap. His counter-statement names no evidence ID and no re-quote; POL-RD-08 provides that assertions from either side that cite no evidence ID carry no weight and are discarded, and that a driver resisting a rider's account must point to a specific artifact and a specific clause. He points to neither, so nothing on his side explains away the 17.5 minutes of empty running that his own trace records.

The rider does not press a route-deviation refund and does not ask the tribunal to find a deviation the trace contradicts. The governing trace figure is 10.8 km against a booked optimal of 10.8 km — an excess of 0.0 km and 0%, below both the 0.8 km and the 20% gates in POL-RD-01 — so no deviation could be established on this trace and an upfront-quoted fare leaves no distance-or-time refund to compute. Her case is not that the car took a longer road; it is that she was billed for a road she was not travelling.

No traffic advisory covers this trip: EV-ADVIS-00714-01 is MISSING, carrying issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight_multiplier 0.0, and its identifier is minted so that the absence itself is citable. There is accordingly no advisory on the record capable of supporting a POL-RD-03 exoneration of the continuation; under POL-RD-13 an external-cause assertion is tested against the advisory for the trip and nothing else, so the only account left on this record for the extra 17.5 minutes is the driver's own admission of an endpoint change. I disclose that this artifact is impaired and at weight 0.0; it is cited for its absence, not for any fact it carries.

The rider is not a serial deviation claimant: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so neither limb of the POL-RD-08 rider-profile factor is engaged and no corroboration-beyond-the-trace requirement attaches to her account. Her claim stands to be weighed on the artifacts, not discounted for a history of claims.

ruling.explanation:
To both of you: this is the dispute over the SGD 16.80 charged for trip TRP-00714. I cannot issue a money ruling on it. The case goes to a human reviewer, and the disputed amount is held rather than collected or refunded. Here is the reasoning, claim by claim.

WHAT THE EVIDENCE SHOWS, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. The GPS trace EV-GPS-00714 covers the whole trip (coverage 100%, no gaps, 10-second sampling) and measures trace_distance_km 10.8 km, identical to the booked optimal of 10.8 km on EV-TRIP-00714. The excess is 0.0 km and 0%. Both POL-RD-01 establishment gates fail, so no route deviation is established on this trace, and the rider does not ask me to find one. The rider's device track (derived.rider_presence on EV-GPS-00714) is static at 0.0 km/h from 11:21:10 — the moment she messaged 'We are getting out here. End our booking at this stop' — through to 11:38:40, while the driver's track ran on to the trip end. On the money, EV-FARE-00714 records fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE, quoted_fare_sgd 16.80 and total_charged 16.80, so charged_over_quote is 0.00; every pass-through and statutory line (erp_total 0.00, airport_surcharge 0.00, waiting_time_fee 0.00) is zero, giving a properly_chargeable total of 0.00. On those figures, taken alone, POL-RD-11 would give the rider no distance-or-time refund (an upfront fare is fixed at booking and an early exit does not reduce it) and POL-RD-09(4) would find no phantom line or wrongly applied surcharge. I accept those points.

WHY THE CASE NEVERTHELESS ESCALATES. EV-TRIP-00714 carries a dropoff amendment timestamp, dropoff_amended_at = 2026-09-24T11:21:10 — the exact moment the rider ended the booking, and the change the driver's own statement concedes ('The booking endpoint was changed at that point, but the app continued recording my car') — but amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are both null. POL-RD-05 provides in terms that where an amendment timestamp is present but amended_optimal_distance_km is null, the re-quote is missing from the record, the clause cannot be run, POL-RD-10(5) applies, and the Judge must not derive a substitute figure. POL-RD-10(5) names this very situation — 'a POL-RD-05 amendment with amended_optimal_distance_km null' — as a mandatory escalation trigger. I therefore cannot re-price the journey that was actually agreed (from the West Grove pickup to the endpoint as amended) and cannot determine what fare is properly chargeable for it. That is a defect in the record, not a finding for either party, and POL-RD-10 escalation is terminal. What would resolve it, and what the reviewer should obtain, is the platform's re-quote for the amended route: amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min for TRP-00714.

THE REMAINING POINTS. The rider's claim that she was billed for a drive she was not on fails under POL-RD-11, which fixes the upfront fare at booking and allows only an over-quote amount (0.00 here) or a POL-RD-09 pass-through correction (none here) — so that limb of her case is rejected on its merits. Her POL-RD-05 argument does not yield a refund either; it is the spring of the escalation, not a payment. The driver's points — no deviation (excess 0.0 km / 0%), upfront fare, no overcharge (charged_over_quote 0.00), no pass-through lines, no billing-integrity defect — are all accepted as far as they go, but none of them cures the missing amended re-quote that POL-RD-05 and POL-RD-10(5) require me to act on. EV-ADVIS-00714-01 is MISSING, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0; no traffic advisory exists for this window, so no POL-RD-03 external-cause exoneration can be run and the driver's endpoint account supplies no amended optimal (POL-RD-13) — that absence is recorded but is not a second escalation ground. On the profile, EV-RPROF-00714 shows deviation_claims_60d = 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated = 0, so the POL-RD-08 corroboration factor is not engaged and the rider's account has not been discounted for claim history. Finally, the chat log EV-CHAT-00714 does record the driver's 11:20:10 message 'Add fifteen for the second person or get down.' That is a conduct matter the reviewer may wish to examine, but no clause in this category produces a referral on these facts — POL-RD-06(c) needs a material deviation and an established pattern, neither of which is present — so I have not added one.

To both parties: this case goes to a human reviewer, and no money moves while it is there. The disputed SGD 16.80 is held — it is not collected from the rider and it is not paid to the driver.

Why it cannot be decided here. Your trip record (EV-TRIP-00714) shows the dropoff point was amended after booking: dropoff_amended_at is 2026-09-24T11:21:10, the same minute the rider messaged 'We are getting out here. End our booking at this stop' (EV-CHAT-00714, MSG-00714-002). But the amended optimal figures are null — amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are both empty. POL-RD-05 says in terms that where an amendment timestamp is present but amended_optimal_distance_km is null, the re-quote is missing from the record, the clause cannot be run, and POL-RD-10(5) applies; the Judge must not derive a substitute figure. POL-RD-10(5) then makes escalation mandatory and terminal, so trigger (5) is what fired. What would resolve it is the platform's stored amended optimal distance and duration for the amended endpoints (or a corrected trip record); that is what the reviewer needs.

What the rest of the evidence shows, so you both know where things sit. On EV-GPS-00714 the trace length is 10.8 km against the booked optimal of 10.8 km on EV-TRIP-00714 — an excess of 0.0 km and 0%. That is below both POL-RD-01 gates (0.8 km and 20% of optimal), so no route deviation is established on this trip. The fare is an upfront quote: EV-FARE-00714 shows fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE, quoted_fare_sgd 16.80 and total_charged 16.80, so under POL-RD-11 POL-RD-02 does not run and no distance-or-time refund is available; charged_over_quote is 0.00. Every pass-through and statutory line is zero — ERP 0.00, airport surcharge 0.00, waiting-time fee 0.00 — so POL-RD-09 has no off-route or phantom line and no surcharge to correct. The rider's early exit (her own device static at 0.0 kph from 11:21:10 on EV-GPS-00714, and her message on EV-CHAT-00714) does not by itself generate a distance refund on an upfront-paid fare. On those grounds alone the merits point to NO_ACTION; the mandatory escalation displaces that ruling because the record cannot be re-priced.

The missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00714-01 is not a second trigger. It is MISSING, carries issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight 0.0, but no party asserted an external traffic cause, so POL-RD-03 was never invoked and POL-RD-13 does not engage.

The driver's in-app demand of SGD 15 for the second passenger (EV-CHAT-00714, MSG-00714-001) is not a line on the ledger — the fare breakdown contains no such charge — so there is nothing to refund for it, and with no repeat-deviation pattern on the driver's profile (deviation_flags_90d is 0) POL-RD-06 produces no conduct referral. That message is a matter the reviewer will see in the file, but no clause turns it into a monetary order on this record.

Net position: escalate and hold the SGD 16.80. No refund and no driver compensation issue on the present record.

Both of you largely agree on what happened, and the artifacts confirm it, so I can separate what is decided from what is not. WHAT IS DECIDED — NO DEVIATION, NO OVERCHARGE. Under POL-RD-01 the governing measurement is the trace (EV-GPS-00714): it runs 10.8 km, exactly the booked optimal of 10.8 km, so the excess is 0.0 km and 0%, below both the 0.8 km and the 20% gates. No deviation is established, and the rider correctly did not press one. The fare (EV-FARE-00714) is an UPFRONT_QUOTE: quoted fare SGD 16.80, charged total SGD 16.80, base fare SGD 3.80, platform fee SGD 0.80, with no ERP gantries, no airport surcharge (this trip neither starts nor ends at an airport) and no waiting-time fee, so the properly chargeable total is SGD 0.00. On an upfront-quoted trip POL-RD-11 fixes the distance and time charges at booking; there is no amount by which the SGD 16.80 charged exceeds the SGD 16.80 quoted, and no pass-through line to correct. The rider's request to refund the SGD 16.80 platform fare because the car later ran empty is refused on those lines: POL-RD-11 does not reduce an upfront fare because the rider disembarks early, and the driver's figures (10.8 km, 20.0 min, SGD 16.80) are correct on the distance and time lines. The claim that no SGD 15 was billed is also correct — the ledger carries no line for the second person. WHY I CANNOT RULE ON THE MONEY. The trip record (EV-TRIP-00714) shows the dropoff point was amended at 11:21:10 — the exact moment the rider messaged 'We are getting out here. End our booking at this stop' (EV-CHAT-00714) — and the driver's own statement confirms the endpoint was changed. But trip_record.amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are both null. POL-RD-05 provides that where an amendment timestamp is present and the amended optimal is null, the re-quote is missing, the clause cannot be run and POL-RD-10(5) applies, and I must not derive a substitute figure. POL-RD-10(5) makes escalation mandatory and terminal. I therefore cannot validate what the SGD 16.80 should have been for the journey as amended, and the disputed SGD 16.80 is held rather than collected or refunded; no monetary outcome issues. OTHER POINTS. The missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00714-01 (status MISSING, weight 0.0) does not change this: no party asserts an external traffic cause citing it, so under POL-RD-13 the absence is a gap in the bundle, not an escalation ground of its own, and it carries no weight as an explanation of the continuation. The rider's profile counters (deviation_claims_60d 0, deviation_claims_60d_substantiated 0) engage no corroboration requirement, and the driver's profile (deviation_flags_90d 0 over completed_trips_90d 250) establishes no repeat-deviation pattern, so no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral arises. FOR THE HUMAN REVIEWER. The open question is the endpoint amendment: what the amended dropoff was, and what the platform would have quoted for it. The driver's in-app demand of SGD 15 from the rider for her companion ('Add fifteen for the second person or get down', MSG-00714-001) and the rider's immediate exit are on the record and are matters the reviewer may wish to examine.

Both parties: this case goes to a human reviewer, so no money moves either way and the SGD 16.80 stays held rather than collected or refunded.

What the record settles. The GPS trace EV-GPS-00714 is complete and unimpaired — 100% coverage, 121 fixes at 10-second sampling, no gaps — and its governing length is 10.8 km, identical to the booked optimal of 10.8 km on EV-TRIP-00714. The excess is 0.0 km and 0%, under both POL-RD-01 gates (0.8 km and 20%), so no route deviation is established. The fare on EV-FARE-00714 is an UPFRONT_QUOTE: the charged total of SGD 16.80 equals the quoted fare of SGD 16.80, charged_over_quote is SGD 0.00, and the properly chargeable pass-through total is SGD 0.00 (no ERP gantries, no airport surcharge, no waiting-time fee). POL-RD-02 does not run on an upfront trip, POL-RD-11 leaves no distance-or-time refund, and POL-RD-09 has no line to correct — the SGD 15 mentioned in the chat appears on no ledger line, so there is no phantom charge. The driver's no-deviation and no-overcharge points are accepted.

Rider's early-exit argument. It is true on EV-GPS-00714 (derived.rider_presence) that your device was stationary at 0.0 kph from 11:21:10 to 11:38:40 while the car kept moving, and true that you messaged 'We are getting out here. End our booking at this stop' at 11:21:10 (EV-CHAT-00714). But on an upfront-quoted fare the distance and time charges were fixed at booking and are not reduced because a rider disembarks early (POL-RD-11), and no ledger line charges you for the driver's demand, so that argument does not by itself produce a refund.

The driver's counter-statement ('the booking endpoint was changed at that point, but the app continued recording my car') asserts an amendment but cites no evidence ID; under POL-RD-08 an uncited assertion carries no weight as a ground, though the amendment is independently recorded on EV-TRIP-00714. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00714-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT; it is cited only for its absence and carries no fact (POL-GEN-02(3)), and POL-RD-03 is unavailable — but no party asserted an external traffic cause, so that absence decides nothing here. The rider's profile shows deviation_claims_60d = 0, so no corroboration-beyond-the-trace requirement attaches (POL-RD-08). No POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral is available: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 and no pattern is established.

Why the case cannot be closed. EV-TRIP-00714 shows the dropoff was amended at 11:21:10 (dropoff_amended_at) — the exact second the rider got out — while amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are both null. POL-RD-05 requires the deviation to be re-measured against the amended endpoints, and where the amendment timestamp is present but the amended optimal is null it directs that the clause cannot be run and POL-RD-10(5) applies; the Judge must not derive a substitute figure. POL-RD-10(5) makes escalation mandatory and terminal. What a human needs is the platform's re-quote for the amended dropoff (amended_optimal_distance_km / amended_optimal_duration_min), or confirmation that none exists, so it can be decided whether the journey priced was the journey booked.
